lastCompletedStory.title: Measure the collapsed check:all and record the numbers durably

nextStoryContext: US-003 was a pure measurement + durable-record story, no source change: the US-001/US-002 collapse of check:all (shared bun test --coverage blob feeding in-process coverage/skip-ratchet gates) was validated as a REAL speedup, not just a green oracle. Measured this cycle, same machine same session: before (fresh git worktree off origin/main, `bun scripts/check-all.ts --json`) = 319s wall-clock, with test/coverage/skip-ratchet each independently re-running the full suite (~92-120s apiece, near-identical durations = the redundant-run fingerprint the issue described). After (this branch, same command) = 105s, with test=98680ms but coverage=15ms and skip-ratchet=0ms (in-process reads of the shared blob). Full CAM-488 bullet with both numbers is now durable in scripts/cam/patterns.md (grep CAM-488). Also reconfirmed check-coverage.ts/check-skip-ratchet.ts still run standalone correctly (their own full suite run, ~90-97s each, exit 0) -- their production adapters were untouched by US-001/US-002 and remain untouched here too. If CAM-488's PRD has further stories, the next one is likely a wrap-up/cleanup story; there is no more coverage/skip-ratchet source work outstanding on check-all.ts itself. Full spine green: bun run typecheck (0 errors), bun test (5942 pass / 0 fail), bun run check:all (exit 0, all 14 gates ok). gate-results.json is a build artifact (gitignored) -- always rm it before committing if a story regenerates it.
